text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementAstronomyCloudy With a Chance of Incineration: Predicting Weather on Distant WorldsHow scientists decode climate light-years awayDNBy David Nield7:00 AM CDT on October 28, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleThe weather on distant planets can tell us a lot about them, including how they formed, what they’re made of, and how likely it is that we might find life there. However, there’s not much meteorological information to go on for celestial objects outside our solar system—they’re basically just flickers of light traveling across the vast emptiness of space.But in a recent study published in Astronomy & Astrophysics, researchers have detailed a new approach to decoding these flickers of light, giving us a better reading on both weather conditions and the drivers of those conditions on faraway worlds.Read more: “Extreme Space Weather Could Delay Your Next Flight”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
